proposedchanges.title: Trade Court Orders Refund Calculations for Importers After Supreme Court Ruling on Trump Tariffs
proposedchanges.description_long:
On March 5, 2026, Judge Richard Eaton of the U.S. Court of International Trade directed Customs and Border Protection to calculate the cost of millions of imports without tariffs the Supreme Court had ruled unlawful. The order began a process for repaying eligible importers with interest; it did not mean refunds had already been paid. For many imports, duties are estimated when goods enter the country and finalized later through liquidation. Eaton directed the agency to finalize affected shipment costs without the disputed tariffs so it could determine the refunds owed.

The ruling followed the Supreme Court’s decision that the tariffs had been collected unlawfully. The court-ordered process must determine how much each eligible importer is owed. The order did not set out when Customs and Border Protection would complete the calculations or how much any company would receive. It is a step toward repayment, not evidence that refunds have already been issued.

evidencebasis: The assigned packet names Judge Eaton, the Court of International Trade, the liquidation process, the Supreme Court ruling, and interest-bearing refunds. The source URLs remain unchanged. The supplied account describes a calculation and repayment process, not completed payments.
